subject: EdgeFin TTFT & streaming integration follow-up
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@edgefin.com>, Nora Patel <nora.p@edgefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: TTFT targets + streaming requirements (next steps)

Hi Liam / Nora —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. This note captures the key performance items we agreed to validate and the immediate next steps so we stay aligned. Short summary: you want a streaming integration (SSE preferred) with strong Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) at load.

Key goals from call:
- TTFT target: p95 <= 200ms under expected peak concurrency (you estimated 30–60 concurrent UI sessions).
- Sustained throughput: ~250 requests/min during peak (bursty patterns, 10–20 requests in short bursts).
- Streaming: SSE preferred for browser clients; fallback to WebSocket for older clients. Chunk cadence: payloads should start delivering first chunk within TTFT and subsequent chunks ideally every 150–300ms for smooth UX.
- Fallbacks: graceful degrade to non-streaming (full response) when streaming not available; preserve partial output.

Attachments I added: quick TTFT checklist and a short note comparing SSE vs WebSocket tradeoffs (redwood-ttft-checklist.pdf / sse-vs-ws-diff.txt).

Next steps (proposed):
1) We (Redwood) will run a small validation profile against your expected traffic: 50 concurrent sessions, sustained 3-minute bursts, latency percentiles and chunk cadence measurement.
2) Engineering sync: loop in Karthik for kernel and batching configuration; Ben will own the integration playbook and sample client code.
3) Share a short sandbox milestone: by Fri 24 Jul we aim to deliver measured TTFT p50/p95 and an example SSE client showing chunk cadence.

Can you confirm the concurrency estimate (30–60) and whether there are clients that must use WebSocket (legacy browser stack)? If you prefer, we can keep the 50-concurrency test as the baseline.

Thanks —
Sofia

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT targets + streaming requirements (next steps)

Thanks Sofia — this is helpful. Quick answers below and a couple of follow-ups: 

- Concurrency: 30–60 is accurate. Our expected peak for the first phase is ~45 concurrent users hitting the feature during end-of-day batch windows.
- WebSocket: A small subset (internal admin UI) still uses an older WebSocket client; majority are modern browsers where SSE is fine.
- Packet cadence: your suggested 150–300ms looks sensible, but our UX lead flagged that anything over 300ms feels chunky for interactive flows. Can you commit to ~200ms median cadence in the test?

Two asks from us: 
1) Can you show how Redwood behaves when there's an upstream model variant switch (e.g., 8-bit quantized fallback) — how does TTFT change and how are chunk boundaries affected?
2) Do you have a recommended request-size limit / token window to ensure TTFT stays low?

If these are fine, we can plan the sandbox run. 

-Liam

Liam —

Great notes. Looping in Karthik (serving/runtime) and Ben (solutions) to answer the two asks and to confirm the baseline test plan. High-level replies before Karthik adds detail: 

- Upstream model variant switch: we support automatic fallback to a lower-precision/quantized variant with a documented TTFT delta. In practice, switching to an 8-bit quantized variant typically increases model compute time by ~5–15% on GPU depending on architecture, but you often gain token throughput. We will include a side-by-side measurement in the sandbox run showing p50/p95 TTFT for each variant.
- Request size / token window: our recommendation for interactive UX is to keep input+expected output token window under ~1,500 tokens for the low-latency path; for longer context we recommend prefix/KV caching and chunked generation. We'll include client-side examples that limit prompt size and stream the rest.

Proposed concrete test baseline (to be executed in our sandbox):
- Concurrency: 50 sessions
- Burst profile: 10s ramp, 3 min sustained burst, 30s cool-down, repeat for 6 cycles
- Workload: average prompt length 300 tokens, expected response 120–300 tokens
- Targets: TTFT p95 <= 200ms; chunk cadence median ~200ms, 95th < 320ms

Karthik / Ben — can you confirm the test harness parameters and whether we should also measure client TCP/TLS handshake variability (Liam: are most clients behind corporate proxies?)

Thanks —
Sofia

Subject: Re: Post-demo: TTFT targets + streaming requirements (next steps)

Hi Liam / Nora —

Thanks for the context. A few pragmatic notes from the runtime side and what we'll measure in the sandbox run. I'll keep it short and actionable.

1) Baseline inference config we will test:
- Model variant: open-arch-large (float16) and open-arch-large-8q (8-bit quant)
- GPU config: 2x A100-like workers with continuous batching enabled
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with max batch window 12ms and batch-size cap tuned to keep TTFT low under 50 concurrency
- KV/prefix caching: enabled for repeated prompts (we'll seed cache to emulate session reuse)

Expected behavior and metrics to collect:
- TTFT: p50/p95 for both variants; expected p95 delta for 8q ~ +10–12% vs float16 on our kernels (we'll verify).
- Chunk cadence: we measure first byte and subsequent chunk intervals. We'll instrument server-side emit timestamps and a client SSE harness to report received chunk timestamps.

2) Network/handshake variance:
- Recommendation: measure cold vs warm TCP/TLS. Cold starts (new TCP/TLS) can add 60–120ms; if your clients commonly open fresh connections per request, that will dominate TTFT. For browser SSE we recommend connection reuse (EventSource) and keep-alives.

3) Fallback strategy:
- Primary: SSE for modern browsers.
- Fallback: WebSocket where SSE unsupported. If both fail, fall back to long-polling JSON (non-streaming).
- When falling back model variants during capacity events, we will send an event metadata header in the stream so the client can mark quality/regression.

4) Client limits suggestion:
- Keep prompt+expected response <= 1500 tokens for the lowest-latency path. For larger contexts use prefix caching and stream incremental generation.

Action items we will deliver in sandbox artifact (by Fri 24 Jul):
- Measured TTFT table for p50/p95 for float16 vs 8q under the 50-concurrency burst profile
- SSE client sample showing median chunk cadence ~200ms and 95th < 320ms (or data showing where we fall short)
- Short runbook: how to configure EventSource vs WebSocket, recommended TLS keep-alive settings, and a small snippet for reconciling partial outputs on fallback.

If the above looks good, Sofia: please share any proxy/network constraints (corporate proxies, gateway termination) so we can include them in the simulation. Liam: once you confirm, Ben and I will schedule the sandbox run and share results + a short readout call.

Thanks —
Karthik
